reported.claim: The loop runs over range(1, number), so it computes the (number-1)th Catalan number instead of the number-th; catalan(2) returns 1 instead of 2.
reported.title: catalan loop range yields the (n-1)th number

reported.claim: The split loop stops one digit too early (range upper bound digits - 1 excludes the split where the right part is the last digit), so Kaprekar numbers whose square's split leaves a single leading digit on the left, such as 9 (81 = 8 + 1), are wrongly reported as not Kaprekar.
reported.title: is_kaprekar split loop stops one digit early

reported.claim: The condition 'not matrix_a or matrix_b' returns an empty list whenever matrix_b is non-empty, so valid non-empty inputs produce [] instead of the Kronecker product.
reported.title: kronecker_product empty check returns [] for non-empty matrix_b

reported.claim: After each row, next_row is assigned the same list object as current_row instead of a copy, so the diagonal read next_row[col+1] sees values already overwritten in the current row, giving an overestimated square size.
reported.title: largest_square_area space-optimized version aliases rows instead of copying

reported.claim: Using true division instead of floor division makes leap_day_reinstall_number fractional, so the calendar arithmetic gives wrong dates for centuries not divisible by 4.
reported.title: gauss_easter uses true division instead of floor division

reported.claim: The loop bound range(3, len(sorted_points) - 1) skips the last sorted point, so the final point is never considered for the hull.
reported.title: graham_scan loop skips the last sorted point

reported.claim: The function divides by molar_mass instead of multiplying, so m2 = m1 * (r1/r2)^2 is computed as (r1/r2)^2 / m1. The doctest value 1.970351 encodes this same error.
reported.title: second_molar_mass divides by molar_mass instead of multiplying

reported.claim: For full groups the code takes the whole remaining suffix arr[i:] instead of the five-element group arr[i:i+5], so the medians are computed over the wrong elements.
reported.title: median_of_medians takes the whole suffix instead of a 5-element group

reported.claim: The comparison checks collection[i - 1] < collection[i] but the swap is applied to positions i and i + 1, so pairs are compared and swapped inconsistently and the wrong element is tested (index -1 wraps around), leaving the list unsorted.
reported.title: odd_even_transposition compares and swaps different pairs

reported.claim: The length test is joined with 'or' instead of 'and', so any 13-digit number is reported valid without checking the check digit.
reported.title: barcode is_valid uses 'or' so 13-digit numbers skip the check digit

reported.claim: The guard `m >= len(text)` returns -1 when the pattern has the same length as the text, even though an exact match at index 0 should be found.
reported.title: bitap_string_match misses a pattern equal in length to the text

reported.claim: When the weighted subtotal is divisible by 10 the checksum becomes 10 instead of 0, so a valid PESEL whose check digit is 0 is rejected.
reported.title: is_polish_national_id yields checksum 10 instead of 0

reported.claim: The function returns the leftover loop variable 'word' (a string) instead of the occurrence dictionary.
reported.title: word_occurrence returns loop variable instead of dictionary

reported.claim: The guard uses `a <= 0`, so a valid non-negative input of 0 is rejected even though the module says only negative values are invalid.
reported.title: binary_or rejects 0

reported.claim: `pbstring.replace(" ", "")` discards its result, so spaces are never removed and a space inside the plugboard string is rejected as an invalid symbol, even though the docstring says pairs can be separated by spaces.
reported.title: _plugboard discards the result of replace, so spaces are rejected

reported.claim: The octet range check is inverted, so it raises for every valid octet in 0..255 and never for out-of-range values.
reported.title: ipv4_to_decimal octet range check inverted

reported.claim: The length counter is decremented (count -= 1) instead of incremented, so len() returns a negative number for a non-empty stack.
reported.title: Stack.__len__ decrements the counter

reported.claim: When a deletion leaves the root with one child, the root merges with that child and takes its prefix, so the root's children are keyed by the wrong characters and words stored under the old child can no longer be found. The root has an empty prefix and must never be merged.
reported.title: RadixNode.delete merges root with its only child, corrupting keys

reported.claim: Elements equal to the pivot are dropped from both partitions, so duplicates of the pivot are lost and the recursion can end on an empty list and crash.
reported.title: kth_number drops elements equal to the pivot

reported.claim: The return value uses the loop variable `w_`, which is never assigned when capacity `w` is 0, so the function raises UnboundLocalError instead of returning the optimal value for an empty capacity; it should return `dp[n][w]`.
reported.title: knapsack raises UnboundLocalError when capacity is 0

reported.claim: The band-count check uses '> 3', so valid 3-band resistors (documented as 3 to 6 bands) are rejected with the 'must be 3 to 6' error.
reported.title: check_validity rejects valid 3-band resistors

reported.claim: The vertical-side linearity check compares v3.y with v2.y instead of v3.x with v2.x, so a valid triangle with two vertices sharing an x-coordinate reaches the slope division and raises ZeroDivisionError.
reported.expected: A Triangle object is constructed without error
reported.title: Triangle.__post_init__ compares y instead of x in the vertical-side check

reported.claim: The visited set is built with set(start), which splits a string node into characters and crashes on non-iterable nodes, so multi-character or integer nodes are handled incorrectly; it should be {start}.
reported.title: bfs_shortest_path_distance builds visited with set(start)

reported.claim: The bounds check validates to_vertex but never from_vertex, so an out-of-range source vertex is not rejected as its docstring intends.
reported.expected: ValueError: Vertex indexes must be in [0; size).
reported.title: AdjacencyList.add_edge does not validate from_vertex

reported.claim: The item's weight is read at weights[counter + 1] instead of weights[counter - 1], so it uses the wrong item and raises IndexError when counter is the last index.
reported.title: knapsack_recur reads weights[counter + 1]

reported.claim: The off-diagonal sum is accumulated with signed values (total -= table[i][j]) instead of absolute values, so a row whose off-diagonal entries are positive is wrongly accepted as diagonally dominant.
reported.expected: A ValueError, since |1| is not greater than |3|.
reported.title: strictly_diagonally_dominant sums signed values instead of absolute values

reported.claim: The elimination loop runs only to num_of_rows - 1, so the last pivot column is never cleared below the diagonal and back substitution then reads non-zero entries that should be zero, giving wrong solutions for 3x3 and larger systems.
reported.title: solve_linear_system elimination skips the last pivot column

reported.claim: The split error is computed by passing the feature array x instead of the label array y to mean_squared_error (the same mistake recurs on lines 79 and 91), so the split is chosen by feature-value spread rather than label error.
reported.failing_call: DecisionTree(depth=2, min_leaf_size=1).predict... after DecisionTree(depth=2, min_leaf_size=1).train(np.array([1, 2, 3, 4]), np.array([0, 0, 10, 10])); tree.predict(4)
reported.title: DecisionTree.train passes x instead of y to mean_squared_error

reported.claim: The vocabulary check uses '>' instead of '>=', so a label equal to vocab_size passes validation and then crashes with an IndexError when building the one-hot filter matrix instead of raising the intended ValueError.
reported.expected: ValueError: Label value must not be greater than vocabulary size.
reported.title: perplexity_loss vocabulary check uses '>' instead of '>='

reported.claim: The epsilon is subtracted inside the square root instead of added, so a zero moving average gives a negative argument to math.sqrt and raises ValueError.
reported.title: rmsprop subtracts epsilon inside the square root

reported.claim: The origin latitude is read from origin[-1] (the longitude) instead of origin[0], so the wrong start point is used.
reported.title: initial_bearing reads origin latitude from origin[-1]

reported.claim: The trapezoid term takes abs of the sum of the two endpoint values before multiplying, so segments where the function changes sign contribute positive area and the result is wrong.
reported.title: trapezoidal_area takes abs of the endpoint sum

reported.claim: Scalar multiplication truncates each product with int(), so non-integer scalars such as 0.5 produce wrong values, and this also corrupts inverse() which multiplies by 1/determinant.
reported.title: Matrix.__mul__ truncates scalar products with int()

reported.claim: The dimension check calls _verify_matrix_sizes, which requires both matrices to have identical shapes, so compatible but non-identical matrix products (e.g. 2x3 times 3x1) are rejected with a broadcast error instead of being multiplied.
reported.title: matrix multiply requires identical shapes

reported.claim: The range stops one short (len - 1), so the summation drops the last resource column and returns one fewer entry than the number of resources.
reported.title: __processes_resource_summation drops the last resource column

reported.claim: The check `tangential_force <= 0` rejects a zero tangential force, so the `elif tangential_force == 0` branch that computes the tangential force is unreachable; it should only reject negative values.
reported.title: shear_stress rejects zero tangential force, making its branch unreachable

reported.claim: The n <= 1 guard is a bare pass instead of a return, so for an empty list block_size becomes 0 and range(0, 0, 0) raises ValueError instead of returning an empty list.
reported.title: kirkpatrick_reisch_sort n <= 1 guard does not return, so an empty list raises ValueError

reported.claim: The zeros bucket is recursed with bit_position + 1 instead of moving down to the next lower bit, so the bit position never reaches 0 and recursion does not terminate for lists whose zero-bucket still has several elements.
reported.title: _msd_radix_sort recurses on the zeros bucket with the wrong bit position

reported.claim: The swap guard uses <=, so equal-length inputs swap and recurse forever instead of falling through to the DP; it should be <, as in levenshtein_distance.
reported.title: levenshtein_distance_optimized swap guard recurses forever on equal lengths
